summary_hint: Borrower LOE from Jordan Rivera dated 07/12/2026 — explains a $25,000 deposit sourced from sale of a vehicle, not borrowed, funds now in Chase ..4471.

typed_core.name: borrower_count
typed_core.why: disambiguator — flags a bad name split

typed_core.name: letter_date
typed_core.why: processor — recency; ties the explanation to a file state

typed_core.name: financial_institution_or_custodian
typed_core.why: processor — where the asset is held (paper-trail anchor)

typed_core.name: account_number_last4
typed_core.why: PII (restricted) — account grouping key to the underlying statement
typed_core.prompt_hint: Keep the account number last-4 only; do not reconstruct a full number even if the letter states it

typed_core.name: asset_type
typed_core.why: processor — checking / gift / sale proceeds / retirement

typed_core.name: asset_issue_type
typed_core.why: identity — what is being explained: large deposit / new account / transfer

typed_core.name: borrowed_funds_indicator
typed_core.why: processor — borrowed funds are ineligible as assets
typed_core.prompt_hint: Borrowed funds (unsecured loans, cash advances) are not acceptable assets unless secured by an owned asset — borrowed_funds_indicator + repayment_obligation_terms are the signal. Capture the explicit statement, do not infer from prose alone

typed_core.name: repayment_obligation_terms
typed_core.why: processor — if borrowed, the repayment liability (DTI)

nested_lists.name: transfer_path_or_chronology
nested_lists.shape_reason: 1–5 hops; flat rows (date, from, to, amount) reconstruct the paper trail. Serves large-deposit sourcing

fields.name: date
fields.why: keeps each amount tied to its transfer step for the paper trail

fields.name: from
fields.why: the origin of the hop in the transfer chain

fields.name: to
fields.why: the destination of the hop in the transfer chain

fields.name: amount
fields.why: the amount moved at this step; stays bound to its date

rejected.name: issuer_name, issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: the borrower is the author; no third-party source

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: borrower_signatures_and_dates covers execution; signature presence is not rule-checked here

rejected.name: borrower_signatures_and_dates
rejected.reason: signature block; attestation carried by borrower_certification; no rule reads individual signatures

rejected.name: supporting_document_list
rejected.reason: a string[] of referenced exhibits; no consumer; catch-all

rejected.name: transaction_or_valuation_dates, amounts_involved
rejected.reason: folded into transfer_path_or_chronology; separate parallel arrays would fragment the trail

encoding_variations: borrowed_funds_indicator — stated as an explicit 'these funds are NOT borrowed', a checkbox, or only implied by the source narrative; capture the explicit statement, do not infer from prose alone

amounts / dates — a letter may state one deposit or a chain of transfers with several amounts and dates; the chronology list keeps each amount tied to its date and step rather than losing them into parallel arrays
asset_issue_type — 'large deposit', 'source of funds', 'new asset', 'cash-out from sale'; drives which sourcing rule would apply

open_questions.q: Chronology vs parallel arrays — amounts_involved (money[]) and transaction_or_valuation_dates (date[]) could be kept as flat scalar lists instead of one object list
open_questions.recommendation: one transfer_path_or_chronology list so each amount stays bound to its date/step; revisit only if letters routinely give a single amount+date (then flatten to two scalars) GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: borrowed_funds_indicator degraded from bool — a tri-state ('yes / no / not stated') is more honest than a bool
open_questions.recommendation: keep as string capturing the stated language

open_questions.q: supporting_document_list — genuinely a list but no consumer
open_questions.recommendation: catch-all rather than a second nested list

notes: No rules consume this type today, so there is no rule floor. An asset LOE exists to source a large deposit / asset for AS-1-style large-deposit sourcing (future). The load-bearing facts are: what is being explained, the origin of funds, whether the funds are borrowed, and the paper trail — plus the last-4 account PII.
PII: account_number_last4 (restricted, pre-masked last-4) maps to the existing account_number_masked registry kind; register/confirm, pre_masked true. Borrower and source-party names are standard.

Prompt hint (doc-level): Large-deposit sourcing (Fannie/Freddie) — a deposit exceeding ~50% of monthly qualifying income generally needs sourcing; the LOE + transfer_path is that source; capture amounts and the paper trail, do not judge sufficiency.
Ambiguity: source_or_origin_of_funds is tagged 'headline' (not a defined reason_class); classified as processor (the explanation the processor consumes).
